_comment: Dependency-provenance gate — the REVIEWED set of packages that carry no
Adding a name here is a REVIEWED EVENT, never a way to make CI green.
Before adding, check whether the package attests at a newer version: an
allowlist reused as a silent pass-through inverts into the opposite of a gate.
Pinned BY NAME, not by count (condition from the 2026-08-14 attestation
audit). Removing a name is safe and encouraged — the gate reports stale
entries as a NOTICE when a package starts attesting.
PLATFORM-BOUND: optional platform packages differ per OS. This list is
derived for the CI runner's platform below; a macOS checkout additionally
installs fsevents and lightningcss-darwin-arm64, which is why the gate
declines to judge off-platform rather than pretending to.
derived_from: npm install --os=linux --cpu=x64 against this repo's committed package-lock.json
policy: registry signatures MUST be 100%; attestation coverage is reported, never enforced as a ratio

_reviewed_additions.lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu: 2026-08-18, first CI run. The CI runner installs this platform binary; a local `npm install --os=linux --cpu=x64` does not resolve it (libc gnu/musl is not simulated by the os/cpu override). Accepted as never-attests on the same basis as its parent `lightningcss`, already pinned here: a project that does not attest its main package does not attest its platform shims, and the 2026-08-14 audit listed lightningcss and its platform shims in the irreducible set. This is a REVIEWED addition, recorded so it is not mistaken for a green-the-build edit.
_reviewed_additions.http-message-sig: 2026-08-23, adding the Web Bot Auth sensor (v1.19.0). Sibling package in the SAME monorepo (cloudflareresearch/web-bot-auth) as `web-bot-auth`, which DOES attest and is the package we deliberately adopted rather than hand-roll RFC 9421. Trusting the parent while refusing a sibling built and released by the same pipeline would be incoherent, not stricter. Checked 2026-08-23: 0.2.0 is the latest version and no version attests, so this is not fixable by upgrading.
_reviewed_additions.jsonwebkey-thumbprint: 2026-08-23, adding the Web Bot Auth sensor (v1.19.0). Same monorepo and same basis as `http-message-sig` above. Direct dependency, used only to derive a JWK thumbprint so a Signature-Input `keyid` can be matched against a published key directory. Checked 2026-08-23: 0.1.0 is the latest version and no version attests.
_reviewed_additions.structured-headers: 2026-08-23, transitive via `http-message-sig`. The reference RFC 8941 structured-headers implementation (evert/structured-header); parsing structured fields is exactly the part of RFC 9421 that must not be hand-rolled. Checked 2026-08-23: installed 2.0.2, latest 2.0.3, neither attests.
